items.title: Section: The Bodhisattva Stage's Second Section Opens — Five True Marks of a Bodhisattva, Each to Be Examined Five Ways

items.zh: 云何真實諸菩薩相？嗢拕南曰：真實諸菩薩，五種相應知，自性、依處、果、次第、攝五轉。謂諸菩薩有五真實菩薩之相，若成就者墮菩薩數。何等為五？一者、哀愍，二者、愛語，三者、勇猛，四者、舒手惠施，五者、能解甚深義理密意。如是五法，當知一一各有五轉。一者、自性，二者、依處，三者、果利，四者、次第，五者、相攝。
items.en:
Within the Basic Section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the second yoga foundation of sustained practice, chapter one: the marks of a bodhisattva.
What are the true marks of a bodhisattva? A summary verse states: "Bodhisattvas' true marks; one should know they are five kinds; intrinsic nature, basis, and fruit; sequence, and inclusion — five turnings."
This means that bodhisattvas have five true marks; anyone who has accomplished them falls within the number of bodhisattvas. What are these five? First, compassion; second, loving speech; third, valour; fourth, open-handed giving; fifth, understanding profound meaning and hidden intent.
One should understand that each of these five factors, in turn, has five further turnings: first, intrinsic nature; second, basis; third, beneficial fruit; fourth, sequence; fifth, mutual inclusion.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Compassion — Both an Inward Wish for Beings' Benefit and Its Actual Expression in Conduct

items.zh: 應知此中，哀愍自性略有二種。一、在意樂，二、在正行。在意樂者，謂諸菩薩，於諸有情利益意樂、安樂意樂，是名哀愍。在正行者，謂諸菩薩，於諸有情如所意樂，隨力隨能身語饒益，是名哀愍。
items.en:
One should understand that, here, compassion's own intrinsic nature is, in brief, of two kinds: first, residing in aspiration; second, residing in actual conduct.
Residing in aspiration means that bodhisattvas hold, towards all sentient beings, the aspiration to benefit them and the aspiration to bring them ease. This is called compassion.
Residing in actual conduct means that bodhisattvas, in accordance with that very aspiration, according to their own strength and capacity, bring concrete benefit to beings through body and speech. This too is called compassion.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Loving Speech, of Valour, and of Open-Handed Giving

items.zh: 愛語自性，謂如前說若慰喻語、若慶悅語、若勝益語，當知如前攝事品說。勇猛自性，謂諸菩薩剛決堅固，無所怯劣，有大勢力。若諸菩薩廣大施性、無染施性，是名舒手惠施自性。
items.en:
Loving speech's own intrinsic nature is, as already explained earlier, comforting speech, joyfully congratulatory speech, and beneficial speech; one should understand this exactly as explained earlier in the Chapter on the Means of Gathering Beings.
Valour's own intrinsic nature is that bodhisattvas are resolute and firm, entirely without timidity or weakness, possessed of tremendous strength.
If bodhisattvas possess both a vast, expansive disposition towards giving and a disposition towards giving free of any taint, this is called open-handed giving's own intrinsic nature.

items.title: Section: Understanding Profound Meaning and Hidden Intent — the Four Kinds of Unobstructed Understanding in Full

items.zh: 若諸菩薩四無礙解，及即於彼無倒引發正加行智，是名能解甚深義理密意自性。
items.en:
If bodhisattvas possess the four kinds of unobstructed understanding, together with the correct, applied wisdom undistortedly brought forth by them, this is called understanding profound meaning and hidden intent's own intrinsic nature.
Commentary: Regarding "if bodhisattvas possess the four kinds of unobstructed understanding" and the like — the bodhisattva's own cultivation of the four kinds of unobstructed understanding has already had its characteristics explained in the chapter on the factors of awakening. Because of this, a bodhisattva is skilfully able to expound the true teaching, giving rise to applied wisdom with respect to all phenomena — this is called the correct, applied wisdom undistortedly brought forth by them.

items.title: Section: The Basis of Compassion Opens — Beings Who Suffer, and Beings Who Delight in Wrongdoing

items.zh: 當知菩薩哀愍依處，略有五種。何等為五？一、有苦有情，二、惡行有情，三、放逸有情，四、邪行有情，五、煩惱隨眠有情。那落迦等所有有情，皆為苦受連綿相續逼切而轉，如是名為有苦有情。或復有情雖非定苦，而多現行諸身惡行、諸語惡行、諸意惡行，於諸惡中喜樂安住。所謂屠養羊猪鷄等不律儀輩。如是名為惡行有情。
items.en:
One should understand that a bodhisattva's basis for compassion is, in brief, five kinds. What are these five? First, beings who suffer; second, beings of wrong conduct; third, heedless beings; fourth, wrongly-practising beings; fifth, beings still latent with affliction.
All beings in the hells and the like are ceaselessly, continuously oppressed and turned about by painful sensation. Such beings are called beings who suffer.
There are also beings who, though not fixed towards suffering, frequently engage in unwholesome conduct of body, unwholesome conduct of speech, and unwholesome conduct of mind, delighting and dwelling contentedly in wrongdoing — such as those undisciplined in conduct who raise and slaughter sheep, pigs, chickens, and the like. Such beings are called beings of wrong conduct.

items.title: Section: Heedless Beings, Wrongly-Practising Beings, and Beings Still Latent With Affliction — Closing the Basis of Compassion

items.zh: 或復有情雖非定苦及行惡行，而於諸欲耽著受用，常樂安住種種俳優、歌舞、笑睇，以自娛樂。所謂一類受欲塵者。如是名為放逸有情。或復有情雖非定苦、行惡、放逸，而依妄見修行種種苦解脫行。謂捨諸欲，於惡說法毘柰耶中而出家者。如是名為邪行有情。或復有情雖非定苦，廣說乃至非修邪行，而或具縛、或不具縛，為諸煩惱之所隨眠。謂正修行賢善異生及諸有學。是名煩惱隨眠有情。是名菩薩所有哀愍五種依處，由此依處、由此所緣，哀愍而轉。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
There are also beings who, though not fixed towards suffering nor engaged in unwholesome conduct, are infatuated with and given over to sensory desires, forever delighting in dwelling amid entertainers, song and dance, and playful glances, amusing themselves. These are beings absorbed in the pleasures of the senses. Such beings are called heedless beings.
There are also beings who, though not fixed towards suffering, unwholesome conduct, or heedlessness, rely on false views to practise all manner of painful paths towards what they take to be liberation — renouncing sensory desires and taking ordination within a wrongly-taught doctrine and discipline. Such beings are called wrongly-practising beings.
There are also beings who, though not fixed towards suffering, and so on up through not practising wrong paths, are nevertheless, whether fully bound or not fully bound, followed by the latent seeds of affliction. These are genuinely practising, wholesome ordinary beings and noble ones still in training. These are called beings still latent with affliction.
Commentary: Regarding "genuinely practising, wholesome ordinary beings" and the like — those who follow through faith or follow through the teaching, heading towards direct contemplation of the truths but not yet having seen the truths, are called genuinely practising, wholesome ordinary beings. Those from the fruit of stream-entry through the path towards arhatship are called noble ones still in training. "Fully bound" and "not fully bound" should be understood as explaining these two in turn, respectively.
These, then, are the bodhisattva's five bases for compassion. It is by depending on these bases, by taking these as objects, that compassion turns and functions. Beyond these five, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.

items.title: Section: The Basis of Loving Speech — Five Kinds of Speech Grounded in the Four Unobstructed Understandings, Closing the Second Mark's Basis in Full

items.zh: 當知菩薩愛語依處，亦有五種。何等為五？一、正言論語，二、正慶悅語，三、正安慰語，四、正廣恣語，五、如理說語。如是廣辯，應知如前攝事品說。是名菩薩所有愛語五種依處，由此依處、由此所緣，愛語而轉。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
One should understand that a bodhisattva's basis for loving speech is likewise five kinds. What are these five? First, correct doctrinal speech; second, correct congratulatory speech; third, correct comforting speech; fourth, correct speech of open, unrestricted generosity; fifth, speech that accords with reason. Their extensive analysis should be understood exactly as explained earlier in the Chapter on the Means of Gathering Beings.
Commentary: Regarding "correct doctrinal speech" and the like — loving speech that discloses the various gateways of the teaching, loving speech that discloses the undistorted characteristics of phenomena, loving speech that discloses the undistorted etymological explanation of the teaching's own language, and loving speech that discloses the undistorted classification of the teaching's own categories, together are called correct doctrinal speech. If a bodhisattva sees that a being's spouse, family, or wealth and grain are flourishing, yet that being remains unaware of it, the bodhisattva, as appropriate, awakens that being to it and expresses congratulations; or, knowing that a being's faith, moral discipline, learning, generosity, or wisdom has increased, likewise offers congratulations. This is called correct congratulatory speech.
These, then, are the bodhisattva's five bases for loving speech. It is by depending on these bases, by taking these as objects, that loving speech turns and functions. Beyond these five, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.

items.title: Section: The Basis of Valour — Five Grounds Already Named in the Chapter on the Factors of Awakening, Three for Others and Two for Oneself

items.zh: 當知菩薩勇猛依處，亦有五種。何等為五？謂即如前菩提分品所說菩薩堅力持性五種依處，當知此是菩薩勇猛五種依處。由此依處、由此所緣，勇猛而轉。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
One should understand that a bodhisattva's basis for valour is likewise five kinds. What are these five? These are exactly the five bases of the bodhisattva's own firm, sustaining resolve already explained earlier in the chapter on the factors of awakening; one should understand that these are valour's own five bases here as well.
It is by depending on these bases, by taking these as objects, that valour turns and functions. Beyond these five, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.

items.title: Section: The Basis of Open-Handed Giving — Five Qualities of Genuine Generosity, From Frequent Giving to Giving Grounded in Nothing at All

items.zh: 當知菩薩舒手惠施，亦五依處。何等為五？一、數數惠施，二、歡喜惠施，三、慇重惠施，四、無染惠施，五、無依惠施。如是五種，如前施品廣辨應知。由此依處、由此所緣，菩薩舒手惠施而轉。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
One should understand that a bodhisattva's open-handed giving likewise has five bases. What are these five? First, frequent giving; second, joyful giving; third, earnest giving; fourth, untainted giving; fifth, ungrounded giving. These five, one should understand, are explained extensively as before in the Chapter on the Perfection of Giving.
Commentary: Regarding "frequent giving" and the like — giving away whatever is obtained the moment it is received, without stinginess, rather than gradually accumulating much wealth over a long time and only then giving all at once, is called frequent giving. Delight before giving, a pure mind while giving, and no regret afterwards is called joyful giving. Giving at the fitting time, not an unfitting one; giving with both giver and recipient genuinely pure, not impure; giving in a manner fitting to the occasion, not unfitting; giving with an undistracted mind, not a scattered one — this is called earnest giving. Giving without a different intention, without a mind agitated and clouded by anger, and giving without clinging to false views and mistaken grasping, is called untainted giving. Giving that does not depend on worldly reputation and praise, does not depend on the recipient's future repayment of kindness, and does not depend on the fruit of becoming Indra, a demon king, a wheel-turning monarch, or one with mastery, is called ungrounded giving. These meanings, one should understand, are as explained in the Chapter on the Perfection of Giving.
It is by depending on these bases, by taking these as objects, that a bodhisattva's open-handed giving turns and functions. Beyond these five, there is nothing to be added and nothing lacking.

items.title: Section: The Basis of Understanding Profound Meaning Opens — the Discourses, and the Twin Depths of Emptiness and Dependent Origination

items.zh: 當知菩薩能解甚深義理密意，亦五依處。何等為五？謂於如來所說契經，隨順甚深甚深顯現空性相應、緣性緣起，應知是名第一依處。
items.en:
One should understand that a bodhisattva's capacity to understand profound meaning and hidden intent likewise has five bases. What are these five? First, the discourses spoken by the tathagata, which accord with and disclose the profound truths of emptiness and of dependent origination. One should understand this is the first basis.
Commentary: Regarding "accord with and disclose the profound" and the like — depth is of two kinds: first, the depth of emptiness; second, the depth of dependent origination. The depth of emptiness means that emptiness's own particular characteristic is neither definitely existent nor definitely nonexistent — this is called according with the profound truth of emptiness. The depth of dependent origination means that, although the links of dependent origination are genuinely impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self, they nonetheless present an appearance resembling permanence and self. This is explained at length in the Stage With Both Investigation and Analysis, and should be understood accordingly. This is called disclosing the profound truth of dependent origination.

blocks.text: Fascicle 47 begins the second part of the Bodhisattva Ground, "the yoga foundation of sustaining the practice according to the Dharma". Its first chapter asks: how can you recognise a true bodhisattva? The answer is five marks, each examined five ways.

Compassion, loving speech, valour, open-handed giving, and understanding profound meaning and hidden intent; "whoever accomplishes them is counted among bodhisattvas". Venerable Miào Jìng: each mark further manifests in five aspects. Master Cháng Bǎi: the last aspect, "inclusion", shows how the five marks and the six perfections include each other.

Venerable Miào Jìng: a bit of compassion that only solves material problems, without seeing the problem in a person's thinking, is not yet a bodhisattva's. Master Cháng Bǎi: through concrete action the bodhisattva changes beings' thinking, turning them from evil to good.

Venerable Miào Jìng: making no distinction between foe and loved one is "vast"; "untainted" means non-grasping. Master Cháng Bǎi: giving with an equal mind, the three spheres empty, is untainted giving.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the four unobstructed understandings are achieved only at the ninth ground; "our little cleverness in explaining some dharma is nothing". Master Cháng Bǎi: to gain them one must cultivate the four investigations and four genuine wisdoms (Day 409).

Suffering beings, beings of wrong conduct, heedless beings, wrongly practising beings, and beings latent with affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first four include ordinary people and outsiders; the fifth includes ordinary and noble Buddhists. Venerable Miào Jìng: suffering alone does not bring liberation; only cutting afflictions does.

Venerable Miào Jìng: like a person asleep in a house, invisible from outside. Insult or praise them and they are not disturbed; the afflictions do not stir, so they are "asleep". Yet they are still there.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "not relying" means not seeking worldly fame or praise in giving.
"The discourses spoken by the Tathāgata, disclosing profound emptiness and dependent origination." Master Cháng Bǎi: 契經 means fitting both the truth and beings' capacities.
Venerable Miào Jìng's sleeping afflictions are worth remembering. A calm day does not mean the afflictions are gone; it may only mean nothing has woken them.

quiz.q: What are the five true marks of a bodhisattva?
options: compassion, loving speech, valour, open-handed giving, understanding profound meaning and hidden intent
quiz.why: Compassion, loving speech, valour, open-handed giving, and understanding profound meaning and hidden intent; whoever accomplishes them is counted among bodhisattvas. Master Cháng Bǎi: fully possessing these five is called the true marks of a bodhisattva.

quiz.q: "Each of the five has five turnings." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "turning"?
options: each mark has five aspects that manifest — "turning" means arising
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: each mark further manifests in five aspects — "turning" means arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: "inclusion" shows how the five marks and six perfections include each other.

quiz.q: Compassion's nature lies in aspiration and in conduct. How do the lectures distinguish a bodhisattva's compassion from ordinary kindness?
options: Miào Jìng: solving only material needs while ignoring their thinking isn't a bodhisattva; Cháng Bǎi: actually changing beings' thinking, turning them from evil to good
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a bit of compassion that only solves material problems, without seeing the problem of their thinking, is not a bodhisattva. Master Cháng Bǎi: through concrete action the bodhisattva truly changes beings' thinking, turning them from evil to good.

quiz.q: Open-handed giving's nature is "vast" and "untainted." How do the lectures explain these?
options: both: no distinction of friend and foe is "vast"; "untainted" is giving without grasping, the three spheres empty
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: making no distinction between foe and loved one is "vast"; "untainted" means non-grasping — grasping is taint. Master Cháng Bǎi: giving with an equal mind, the three spheres empty, accomplishes untainted giving.

quiz.q: The nature of understanding profound meaning is the four unobstructed understandings. At which ground does Venerable Miào Jìng say they are achieved?
options: only at the ninth ground — our little cleverness in explaining a bit of dharma is nothing
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: among the ten grounds, the four unobstructed understandings are achieved only at the ninth; our little cleverness in explaining some dharma is nothing. Master Cháng Bǎi: to gain them one must cultivate the four investigations and four genuine wisdoms.

quiz.q: Which five kinds of beings are the basis of a bodhisattva's compassion?
options: the suffering, the wrongdoers, the heedless, the wrongly practising, those latent with affliction
quiz.why: Suffering beings, beings of wrong conduct, heedless beings, wrongly practising beings, and beings latent with affliction. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first four include ordinary people and outsiders; the fifth includes ordinary and noble Buddhists.

quiz.q: For "beings latent (隨眠) with affliction," what image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for "sleeping"?
options: like someone asleep inside a house, unseen; insult or praise stirs nothing — the afflictions don't move
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: like a person sleeping in a house, invisible from outside; insult or praise them and they're not disturbed — the afflictions don't stir, so they're "asleep."

quiz.q: Among the five bases of giving, which one gives without relying on fame or return?
quiz.why: "Ungrounded giving." Venerable Miào Jìng: "not relying" means not seeking — not seeking worldly fame or praise in giving.
